Getting ready for a first call

What to bring to a free 15-minute call with neon1.

Type
Guide
Edition
1.1
Published
November 9, 2026
For
Anyone thinking about a project
Download PDF Preview PDF (opens in a new tab)
On this page 4 sections
  1. Bring one real example
  2. Five questions to think about
  3. Have nearby, but don't send
  4. What you'll leave with

The first call is free and short, about 15 minutes. Its job is to find the main pain point and whether I'm the right help. A little preparation helps.

Bring one real example

The most useful thing to bring is the last time the problem happened. Not "our intake is messy," but "on Tuesday a referral sat in the inbox for three days." Real examples show where the work waits.

Five questions to think about

  1. What happens, step by step, from start to finish?
  2. How often does it happen, and roughly how long does it take?
  3. What goes wrong, and what do people do when it does?
  4. What must not change, such as a system you're keeping or a way customers reach you?
  5. What would "fixed" look like to you?

You don't need exact numbers. "About 40 a week, maybe 5 minutes each" is plenty.

Have nearby, but don't send

  • A list of the tools and subscriptions involved
  • Who owns or administers each account
  • Who else should be part of the conversation, especially the person who does the work every day

Please don't send passwords, health details, or payment information, before the call or during it. If the work involves health information, we'll go through the business associate agreement request before any access.

What you'll leave with

  • A plain description of the problem
  • A few options, including doing nothing and using what you already have
  • Whether I'm a good fit, and if not, who might be
  • The smallest useful next step, if there is one

After the call, you'll get a short proposal with options and estimates if it makes sense. Nothing starts until you pick one. The intake form is what I fill in from our conversation.

Book a call or see contact for other ways to reach me.
